claim: The paper gives an explicit closed-form formula for A_2(p), the number of numerators a for which a/p has a length-2 Egyptian fraction representation, and a parametrization of length-3 Egyptian fractions yielding bounds for A_3(n), f_a(n), and F(n).
stance_target: state of the art on counting three-term (length-3) Egyptian fraction representations
quoted_support: we give a formula for A_2(p) and a parametrization for Egyptian fractions of length 3, which allows us to give bounds to A_3(n), to f_a(n) = #{(m_1,m_2,m_3): a/n=1/m_1+1/m_2+1/m_3}, and finally to F(n) = #{(a,m_1,m_2,m_3): a/n=1/m_1+1/m_2+1/m_3}.

claim: The f_a(n) counting function defined in this paper -- the multiplicity of representations of a SINGLE fixed rational a/n as a sum of three unit fractions -- is structurally the building block a birthday-paradox heuristic for Section 5's coincidence-counting problem would need, but this paper counts single triples per value, not coincidences between the triple-sets of two different values.
stance_target: whether existing counting machinery transfers to the equal-sum-and-equal-reciprocal-sum pair problem
scope_conditions: length-3 Egyptian fraction representations of a single rational a/n
quoted_support: Let a,n be positive integers that are relatively prime. We say that a/n can be represented as an Egyptian fraction of length k if there exist positive integers m_1, ..., m_k such that a/n = 1/m_1+ ... +1/m_k.
